lines.en: Good morning. What seems to be the problem today?

pages.title: A obra e a situação

work.title: A Modest Proposal
work.note: A Modest Proposal é um ensaio satírico de Jonathan Swift, publicado em 1729, que apresenta um argumento passo a passo, em tom irônico, para criticar a pobreza na Irlanda. A argumentação em ordem combina com organizar uma fala. A cena é autoral; não adapta nem cita a obra. A referência é um ensaio com argumentos em ordem: to begin with.

items.wrong: I have a fever since Monday.
items.fix: I’ve had a fever since Monday.
items.why: Com since use o present perfect: I’ve had.

items.wrong: I’ve felt dizzy since two days.
items.fix: I’ve felt dizzy for two days.
items.why: Use for com período e since com ponto de partida.

items.wrong: How long you have a cough?
items.fix: How long have you had a cough?
items.why: Use have you had na pergunta.

teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.
solo: Pergunte por que o erro acontece em português e como evitar.
group: Compare erro e forma natural: I have a fever since Monday. → I’ve had a fever since Monday. | I’ve felt dizzy since two days. → I’ve felt dizzy for two days. | How long you have a cough? → How long have you had a cough?.
Peça que digam a forma natural em voz alta.
extra90: Cada aluno cria um erro típico seu e o grupo corrige.

facts.label: Present perfect com for e since
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio com for (período) e since (início): I’ve had a fever for two days, since Monday.

facts.label: há + tempo
facts.sub: Use for com um período de tempo: for two days, for a week, for a while. I’ve had a fever for two days. Depois de for vem uma duração, não uma data.

facts.label: desde + ponto
facts.sub: Use since com o início do período: since Monday, since yesterday, since last night. I’ve had a headache since yesterday. Depois de since vem um ponto no tempo.

compare.ask: I’ve had a fever for two days.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “estou com febre há dois dias” e “estou com dor desde ontem”, no presente.
compare.tip: Diga: “I’ve had a fever for two days.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use o present perfect com for e since: I’ve had a fever for two days. I’ve had a headache since yesterday. For = período; since = ponto de partida. Não diga “I have a fever for two days”.

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: I’ve had a fever for two days.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: For is used with a period of time, like two days.
Since is used with two days.
items.why: Since is used with a starting point, like Monday.

items.s: I’ve felt dizzy all day is present perfect.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

answers: For is used with a period of time, like two days. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
Since is used with two days. → Falso (Since is used with a starting point, like Monday.)
I’ve felt dizzy all day is present perfect. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A visit to a clinic in Toronto · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a cold morning in Toronto. Nina feels very tired and weak. She has not slept well for two nights. She walks into a small clinic. Dr. Gus is ready to see her. He has worked here since 2015.
“Good morning. What seems to be the problem today?” says Gus. “I’ve felt dizzy all day, and I’ve had a headache since yesterday.” says Nina. “How long have you had a fever?” says Gus.
